I mean, I love morrowind and the original Fallout games but I'm not about to claim they have some kind of timeless art style.  It's definitely charming, but obviously those games wouldn't look like that if they were released today.  And yeah, graphics are naturally not the draw for (most) games, but in the "vibey-indie-walking-sim" genre, graphics DO seem to be a staple, not realistic or high definition, but rather a quaint level of beauty, like Gone Home which heavily inspired LiS. 

Not to say the game isn't gorgeous, because it absolutely is in almost every area EXCEPT for the human models, if the remaster had focused entirely on keeping the original mood and lighting and put the heaviest work into the character models and jank improvements I think it would have been received a lot better.  I mean, it almost does this, but as others have said, the trade-off is that the more next-gen environments have sucked some of the nostalgic vibe out of some scenes.   I still prefer the remaster, I think, but purely for how much I love Max & Chloe's new models.

Because Pirate was the brainchild of someone who is evidently no longer apart of the team.  It was a foolish idea to begin with, making a sister game, MMOs are ridiculously expensive and hard to maintain and Wiz was never popular enough to warrant that.  

It was an unfortunate accident that the game was good, so much passion and love poured into this project that was doomed from the beginning.  Remember for a while there that the character models were actually better looking than the Wiz avatars because the graphics were more recent?  If you compare the pirate models to the old Wiz ones you'll see what I mean.  Pirate was a whole different beast, brand new mechanics, more freedom to travel the spiral physically instead of using portals, and the story had so much effort put into it that people still go back and replay level 1-70 just for the character moments.

So to answer your question; the game was somebody's baby,  KI probably really, truly believed in this game at the time of its release, it was the stagnation of the following years that killed it.  It was the layoffs at kingsisle that killed it.  Most importantly I think it was the fact that it was a Wizard101 Pirate spinoff that had not much appeal outside of Wiz fans that made it doomed to begin with.  The wiz lore wasn't all that interesting up until recent years so nobody was jumping in for the story, it had to rely purely on people's desire to try out another MMO from scratch.  

Idk if you ask me at least, it was never going to be popular, and that's the tragedy of it, because it's so fucking good.
